Very thorough read-only audit of /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa for building a "Recently Viewed" horizontal product rail (SFCC-83) and a "Full History" page (SFCC-84). Report FACTS with file:line citations. If something does not exist, say so explicitly — do not infer.

Answer each numbered question separately:

1. **Existing carousel / rail / horizontal-scroll infrastructure.** Search `overrides/app/components/` (especially `ui-kits/`) for any existing carousel, slider, rail, scroller, or horizontal-list component. Also check whether `@salesforce/retail-react-app`'s base `recommended-products` / `product-scroller` components exist in node_modules and whether either is already overridden in `overrides/`. Report exact paths and whether each has a `.css.ts` recipe, story, test.

2. **`ZimmProductCard` contract.** Read `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/index.tsx` in full. Report: the exact `variation` union members; the full prop list per variation (required vs optional); the complete `VARIATION_CONFIG` table (every flag and its value per variation); and quote verbatim any docblock comment mentioning "recently viewed" or "Recently Viewed".

3. **Browsing-history / persistence.** Search the whole repo for any existing recently-viewed, view-history, or browsing-history logic: `grep -ri "recently.viewed\|recentlyViewed\|viewHistory\|browsingHistory\|recently_viewed"`. Also check `overrides/app/hooks/` for any localStorage/sessionStorage persistence hook, and search for `localStorage`/`sessionStorage` usage anywhere in `overrides/`. Report what exists.

4. **Einstein / recommendations wiring.** Does `overrides/app/hooks/use-einstein.ts` exist? Read it. Does it expose any "viewed products" or `sendViewProduct`-style call? Is it currently called anywhere in `overrides/`? Also check `node_modules/@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` for any `useShopperCustomers` / customer-productlist API that could store per-customer history.

5. **Consent / Didomi.** Search all of `overrides/` and `config/` for `didomi`, `consent`, `Didomi`. Report whether ANY consent-gating mechanism exists today.

6. **Routing & pages.** Read `overrides/app/routes.tsx`. List the existing route entries and note how a new page route would be added. List every directory under `overrides/app/pages/`.

7. **Tier check.** For each of these, quote the matching entry (or state "not listed") from `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md` and `.claude/rules/protectedFiles.md`: `overrides/app/routes.tsx`; `overrides/app/components/recommended-products/`; `overrides/app/hooks/use-einstein.ts`; `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts`; `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/**`; `overrides/app/pages/**`.

8. **Nearest existing pattern for a new organism.** List every directory under `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/`, `.../molecules/`, `.../organisms/`. For ONE representative organism that has all four files, list its exact file set.

Be precise and exhaustive. Cite file:line.

253	  hoverHidesPrice: boolean;

291	  home: {
292	    showBag: false,
293	    showAttributes: false,
294	    showSizeChips: false,
295	    hoverHidesPrice: false,
296	    hoverRevealsPrice: true,
297	    hoverRevealsSizeSelector: false,

299	    hideBagOnMobile: false,

301	    showBadge: false,
302	    showHoverImageSwap: false,

305	    showBag: true,
306	    showAttributes: false,
307	    showSizeChips: true,
308	    hoverHidesPrice: true,
309	    hoverRevealsPrice: false,
310	    hoverRevealsSizeSelector: true,
311	    showRemove: false,
312	    hideBagOnMobile: true,
313	    hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable: false,
314	    showBadge: true,
315	    showHoverImageSwap: true,
316	  },

318	    showBag: true,
319	    showAttributes: true,
320	    showSizeChips: true,
321	    hoverHidesPrice: true,
322	    hoverRevealsPrice: false,
323	    hoverRevealsSizeSelector: true,
324	    showRemove: true,
325	    hideBagOnMobile: false,
326	    hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable: true,
327	    showBadge: true,
328	    showHoverImageSwap: true,

332	const messages = defineMessages({
333	  // Interpolated with the product name, matching ZimmProductPrice's WAS/NOW pattern — Media's
334	  // own `removeLabel` prop is a plain string, so the interpolation happens here, at the one call

336	  removeFromWishlist: {

338	    defaultMessage: 'Remove {name} from wishlist',
339	  },

342	const ZIMM_PRODUCT_CARD_RECIPE = 'ZimmProductCard';
343	
344	/**
345	 * Organism — the full product card, composing `ZimmProductCardMedia` and `ZimmProductCardContent`
346	 * across the `home` / `plp` / `wishlist` variations. See the module docblock above for the
347	 * confirmed Figma variation matrix and this component's own recipe (`zimmProductCard.css.ts`) for
348	 * the stretched-link and hover-reveal mechanics that live entirely in CSS, not in this render
349	 * body — both children are always rendered in full, with every one of their own sub-parts; CSS
350	 * alone decides what is visible for a given variation and pointer capability.
351	 *
352	 * @param props see `ZimmProductCardProps` — a discriminated union on `variation`.
353	 */
354	export const ZimmProductCard = (props: ZimmProductCardProps) => {
355	  const {
356	    id,
357	    href,
358	    name,
359	    headingLevel,
360	    primaryImage,
361	    hoverImage,
362	    images,
363	    currentPrice,
364	    originalPrice,
365	    isPriceLoading,
366	    isUnavailable,
367	    onNotifyMe,
368	    badge,
369	    variation,
370	  } = props;
371	
372	  const { onAddToBag, sizeChipValues, selectedSizeChipValue, onSizeChipSelect, colour, size, onRemove } =
373	    props as ZimmProductCardVariationFields;
374	
375	  const intl = useIntl();
376	  const config = VARIATION_CONFIG[variation];
377	
378	  // Both conditions required — an organism that sets isUnavailable without a real callback
379	  // should not show a dead notify-me button. Mirrors ZimmProductCardContent's own
380	  // showNotifyMeButton co-requirement.
381	  const showNotifyMe = Boolean(isUnavailable) && Boolean(onNotifyMe);
382	
383	  // Fix C (SFCC-236 Step 6 visual audit): confirmed against the real Figma Default+Hover
384	  // instances for every variation × Unavailable=True (including the Mobile/no-hover variants,
385	  // which show the only state a touch pointer ever sees) that `isUnavailable` suppresses the
386	  // size-selector hover-swap entirely — there is nothing to pick for an out-of-stock item, so
387	  // price stays visible on hover instead of being replaced. Home's own hover-reveals-price
388	  // behaviour is untouched by this — Home's Unavailable Hover reference (node 40002163:39990)
389	  // still reveals price on hover exactly as the in-stock case does; only the PLP/Wishlist
390	  // hide-and-swap needs suppressing.
391	  //
392	  // Suppressing `hoverRevealsSizeSelector` alone is not enough to reproduce that reference: it
393	  // only stops the organism adding its OWN hide/reveal pair, which leaves the size-chip wrapper
394	  // at Content's own natural (visible) default — briefly shipped that way mid-fix and caught by
395	  // re-checking the real Storybook render against Figma, which confirms size chips stay hidden
396	  // in BOTH states when unavailable, not just "not swapped in on hover". `sizeSelectorUnavailable`
397	  // carries that permanent hide separately, unconditional (not gated by hover-capability at all —
398	  // this isn't a pointer-type concern, unlike everything else in this recipe).
399	  //
400	  // Follow-up (full-sweep visual audit against every variant x state node, not just the sampled
401	  // set the first pass checked): `sizeSelectorUnavailable` ALSO drives a mobile-only price hide
402	  // in the recipe now (Fix F) — confirmed via `get_metadata` that Mobile PLP/Wishlist Unavailable
403	  // hide price and show notify-me in its place (`40002163:41488`, `40002187:58475`), the OPPOSITE
404	  // of Desktop's additive treatment (price stays, notify-me is simply added on hover). Nothing
405	  // extra is computed here for it — the recipe reads the same `sizeSelectorUnavailable` boolean
406	  // for both the size-chip permanent-hide and this new price rule, since both only ever apply to
407	  // the same PLP/Wishlist-and-unavailable case.
408	  const hoverHidesPrice = config.hoverHidesPrice && !isUnavailable;
409	  const hoverRevealsSizeSelector = config.hoverRevealsSizeSelector && !isUnavailable;
410	  const sizeSelectorUnavailable = config.hoverRevealsSizeSelector && Boolean(isUnavailable);
411	
412	  // Fix G (same follow-up audit): Wishlist-only. `hideBagOnMobile` alone only covers PLP's own
413	  // unconditional mobile hide; Wishlist's bag stays visible on mobile UNLESS unavailable
414	  // (`40002187:58470` vs `40002187:58473`). Combined into one boolean here rather than exposing
415	  // both conditions to the recipe — it only needs to know "hide this on mobile for this render",
416	  // not why.
417	  const bagHiddenOnMobile = config.hideBagOnMobile || (config.hideBagOnMobileWhenUnavailable && Boolean(isUnavailable));
418	
419	  const removeLabel = config.showRemove ? intl.formatMessage(messages.removeFromWishlist, { name }) : undefined;
420	  const resolvedBadge = config.showBadge ? badge : undefined;
421	
422	  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_PRODUCT_CARD_RECIPE, {
423	    hoverHidesPrice,
424	    hoverRevealsPrice: config.hoverRevealsPrice,
425	    hoverRevealsSizeSelector,
426	    sizeSelectorUnavailable,
427	    // Same Fix C audit: notify-me is hover-gated on hover-capable devices (hidden by default,
428	    // revealed on hover/focus-visible — every Desktop Unavailable+Hover reference shows it
429	    // appearing only there) but unconditionally visible on touch (every Mobile Unavailable
430	    // reference — the only state a touch pointer ever sees, per the "Mobile has no Hover variant"
431	    // finding — shows it plainly, with no hover to reveal it). This flag is deliberately keyed off
432	    // `showNotifyMe` itself, not `variation`: the confirmed behaviour is identical across all
433	    // three variations, and the recipe's selector simply matches nothing when notify-me isn't
434	    // mounted at all.
435	    hoverRevealsNotifyMe: showNotifyMe,
436	    hideBagOnMobile: bagHiddenOnMobile,
437	  });
438	
439	  return (
440	    <chakra.div __css={styles.root} data-testid="product-card" data-product-id={id}>
441	      <ZimmProductCardMedia
442	        primaryImage={primaryImage}
443	        hoverImage={hoverImage}
444	        images={images}
445	        swapOnHover={config.showHoverImageSwap && Boolean(hoverImage)}
446	        showControls
447	        badge={resolvedBadge}
448	        onRemove={onRemove}
449	        removeLabel={removeLabel}
450	      />
451	      <ZimmProductCardContent
452	        name={name}
453	        headingLevel={headingLevel}
454	        href={href}
455	        currentPrice={currentPrice}
456	        originalPrice={originalPrice}
457	        isPriceLoading={isPriceLoading}
458	        showAttributes={config.showAttributes}
459	        colour={colour}
460	        size={size}
461	        showBag={config.showBag}
462	        isUnavailable={isUnavailable}
463	        onAddToBag={onAddToBag}
464	        showSizeChips={config.showSizeChips}
465	        sizeChipValues={sizeChipValues}
466	        selectedSizeChipValue={selectedSizeChipValue}
467	        onSizeChipSelect={onSizeChipSelect}
468	        showNotifyMe={showNotifyMe}
469	        onNotifyMe={onNotifyMe}
470	      />
471	    </chakra.div>
472	  );
473	};
474	
475	export default ZimmProductCard;

102	personal credential (Jira/Confluence token, Contentful CMA token) into the centrally-shared
103	store instead of keeping it local-only — see the `scope:personal` handling documented in
104	`.env.sample`'s header before changing the scope-parsing logic.

110	
111	These files define the Zimmermann content model, authored once as a single
112	organization-scoped Contentful **Environment Template** (`npm run sync:contentful`,
113	via `client.environmentTemplate.*` in the `contentful-management` SDK) and installed
114	into each environment (`npm run install:contentful -- --target <env>`). This replaced
115	an earlier per-environment `sync.js` + migration-file pipeline once Contentful moved to
116	recommending organization-level content models over independently-synced
117	space/environment content types.

119	`content-types/*.js` is the sole source of truth per content type (including
120	`localized`/`required`/`validations` — there is no longer a separate migration file that
121	overrides an inferior default). Field deletion during an install is opt-in
122	(`--delete-deleted-fields`), off by default — a mistaken field definition pushed to the
123	production Contentful environment is difficult to undo and may break running components.

Split out of [conventions.md](./conventions.md) — see that file for cross-cutting rules that apply to every file regardless of type (TypeScript-only, DRY/KISS/SOLID, magic numbers, security). TypeScript idioms live in [typescript.md](./typescript.md); Chakra/CSS conventions live in [css.md](./css.md). --- ## Components - **Named export** matches the folder name (e.g. `productTile/` exports `ProductTile`). No default exports of anonymous functions. - **Props type name** matches the component name: `ProductTileProps` for `ProductTile`, `TopNavProps` for `TopNav`. - **Props type placement:** - _Default:_ declare the `Props` type at the top of the component file. - _Move to `types.ts` in the same folder_ only when (a) the type is consumed by sibling files (story, test, sub-components) **or** (b) it exceeds ~30 lines and mixes with other shared types worth co-locating. - The trigger is _shared consumption_, not line count alone. - **JSDoc** is required on: - Any component used by ≥2 callers (shared components — typically Tier 2 in [protectedFiles.md](./protectedFiles.md)). - Any exported hook. - Any utility function with non-obvious behaviour. Leaf components used by a single page don't need JSDoc — the prop type is sufficient. - **Callback props** follow `onEventName` (e.g. `onAddToCart`, `onClose`). - **Required props are non-optional;** optional props use `?` — no `| undefined` unions for "I forgot to mark it optional." - **Accessibility (JSX) — mechanically enforced by `.coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/`, so get these right at authoring time:** - Every `` needs an `alt` attribute (`alt=""` is fine for purely decorative images). - Every `IconButton` (including wrapped variants like `IconButtonWithRegistration`) needs an `aria-label` — it renders no visible text, so screen readers have nothing else to announce. - Any element with an `onClick` that isn't natively interactive (`div`, `span`, `Box`, `Flex`, `Stack`, `VStack`, `HStack`, `Grid`, `Text`, and similar) needs a `role` attribute at minimum — and for real keyboard operability, also `tabIndex={0}` and an `onKeyDown` handler (or just use a `Button`/native interactive element instead, which is almost always simpler than reimplementing keyboard behaviour). --- ## Composition — writing a "clean" component Rules of thumb for when a component is doing too much and should be split, or when inline state belongs in a custom hook instead. - **Complexity / size.** A component function should stay roughly under ~150 lines and avoid deep branching (rule of thumb: ~10-15 cyclomatic complexity — count independent paths through the render logic, not total lines). **This is not currently ESLint-enforced** — `.eslintrc.js` has no `max-lines-per-function` or `complexity` rule configured today, so treat this as a self-check during authoring and something `/code-quality` should flag, not something the build will fail on yet. If this keeps being a problem in practice, adding those two ESLint rules is a cheap follow-up (they're built into ESLint core, no new dependency needed). - **Container/presentational separation.** Anything under `overrides/app/components/` receives data as props — it does not call data-fetching hooks itself (SDK hooks like `useCurrentBasket`/`useCurrentCustomer`/`useProduct`, or any `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` / React Query hook). Data-fetching belongs in `overrides/app/pages/` or another container component, which then passes the result down. This generalizes the existing "no commerce state hooks inside leaf components" rule to _all_ data-fetching, not just commerce SDK hooks — the reasoning is the same either way: a component that owns its own data-fetching can't be reused somewhere the data arrives differently (SSR-prefetched, mocked in Storybook, composed from a parent that already has it).
